13.text: The Ravishing of Women. — The ravishing of women was frequent in

14.text: older, more warlike times. In the tales, however, the ravishing is almost

15.text: always performed by men of other tribes, by Taˊn˙ñɪt,² by spirits, also by an

16.text: eagle, a whale, a raven, etc.

17.text: One of the tales, that about Eleˊndi and his sons, gives a very character-

18.text: istic description of the ravishing of women.

19.text: “(There were) five brothers and two sisters. When the girls were taking water, their ear-ornaments

20.text: jingled, also the numerous bracelets of metal on their arms from the wrist to the elbow. They

21.text: lingered, taking water, and began to laugh among themselves. Their braided hair hung down on

22.text: both sides. Two young men approached stealthily along the river-bank. They caught them both:

23.text: each man caught one girl. ‘Go with us!’ they exclaimed. The girls refused. The ravishers

24.text: brandished their spears over the girls’ heads. Then they were afraid and followed them. One of

25.text: the Taˊn˙ñɪn ravishers said, ‘We will take this road; but mind you do not try to escape!’ The

26.text: girls could not walk, because, being of a rich family, they were not accustomed to go afoot. They

27.text: sat down on the ground, and the men with them.

28.text: “Every one is asleep. The sisters, however, can neither sleep nor walk. Their feet are sore;

29.text: they yearn for their home. The men sleep on. Not far ahead, there is visible, under a cliff, a

30.text: large snow-drift, old and hard, hardened by summer wind. One sister says to the other, ‘Let us

31.text: flee to that snow, and let us try to burrow in it. They can go home by themselves; otherwise

32.text: they will kill us; we are unable to walk any longer.’

33.text: “The older sister took the knife from one of the sleeping men. They went to the snow, cut

34.text: it through with the knife, and dug the ground under it, making a hole like a fox’s burrow. The

35.text: elder sister made the younger go in, then covered her with earth and snow, and effaced all traces

36.text: of her work, as if the snow were quite intact. While working thus, she said, ‘I will go with them.

37.text: You at least, shall return home. While they are here, you must remain quietly in hiding; but

38.text: when the sun is quite high, and we go away, all three of us, then you may come out and return

39.text: home. The younger of the brothers wants very strongly to have me for his wife. Let him take

40.text: me, but you go home.’ She went back to the men, put the knife in its old place; then, lying

41.text: down, she simulated sleep. When the spring sun began to descend, one of the men awoke, then

42.text: another. ‘Oh, dear! where is the other girl? She has fled, and we did not notice it.’ The other

43.text: girl continues to feign sleep. They try to wake her, but still she sleeps. At last she awakens too.

44.text: ‘Where is the other? Ah! but she was lying here close by! What have you done with her? You

45.text: have slept side by side!’ — ‘Oh, but you are men! Why have you not had a look for her? I

46.text: was so tired, I could not even walk. But why have you slept so soundly?’ The men were silent.
